editor_note: Entries 28 and 32 are accurate and read naturally. The DAG round-trip ("diproses dalam bentuk DAG") and the layer-by-layer SWAP insertion ("jalur swap ditentukan dan Gate SWAP yang diperlukan disisipkan") both keep the English meaning, with nothing dropped or inverted. The only problem is in entry 38: in the last recommendation, the sentence-final period moved inside the link text ("[Dokumentasi API DAG Circuit.]"), so it becomes part of the link label. The list items are also indented 4 spaces where the English has none. Neither of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: - Review the [DAG Circuit API documentation](https://docs.quantum.ibm.com/api/qiskit/dagcircuit).
examples.translation: - Tinjau [Dokumentasi API DAG Circuit.](https://docs.quantum.ibm.com/api/qiskit/dagcircuit)
examples.suggested: - Tinjau [dokumentasi API DAG Circuit](https://docs.quantum.ibm.com/api/qiskit/dagcircuit).
examples.why: The period has moved inside the link text, so it becomes part of the link label. It should come after the closing parenthesis, as in the English. The unexpected 4-space indent on the list items should also be removed to match the source.

editor_note: Rewritten entry 13 is faithful and natural: "merilis dua model baru sebagai open source untuk inferensi lokal di Hugging Face" keeps the count (two), "local inference", and the open-sourcing claim intact, and it reads idiomatically.

I only judged the two rewritten entries, and both say what the English says. Entry 9 ("mempercepat dan memperbaiki skalabilitas pemilihan layout circuit-ke-hardware, mengurangi overhead kompilasi dan meningkatkan fidelitas") keeps all the claims without weakening or strengthening any of them. Entry 6 has one awkward phrase: "yang berfokus pada menempatkan Qiskit sebagai platform terdepan" puts "pada" before a verb, which reads like a translation. A native editor would write "yang berfokus untuk menjadikan Qiskit…". "Berlandaskan momentum" is also a little stiff, and "Melanjutkan momentum" would sound more natural.

examples.source: which has centered on positioning Qiskit as the leading platform
examples.translation: yang berfokus pada menempatkan Qiskit sebagai platform terdepan
examples.suggested: yang berfokus untuk menjadikan Qiskit sebagai platform terdepan
examples.why: 'berfokus pada' followed by a verb ('menempatkan') is copied from the English structure and sounds awkward. 'berfokus untuk menjadikan' is how an Indonesian technical writer would say it.

examples.source: Building on the momentum established across the v2.x series
examples.translation: Berlandaskan momentum yang telah terbangun sepanjang seri v2.x
examples.suggested: Melanjutkan momentum yang terbangun sepanjang seri v2.x
examples.why: 'Berlandaskan momentum' is a literal rendering of 'building on'. 'Melanjutkan momentum' is the more natural Indonesian way to say it.

editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries (23, 26, 32, 54, 55) misleads a learner. They keep the "cannot change interactive TTL / must be less than system maximum" constraint, the "whichever happens last" rule, and the 5-lane / 2-occupied / 6-job example unchanged. The main issue is entry 23: it opens with "Anda" and then switches to "administratormu" and "kamu" in its last sentence, while the rest of the page consistently uses "Anda". A smaller issue is entry 32's "waktu jam dinding", a literal calque of "wall clock time". It is understandable, but a native technical writer would more likely write "waktu nyata (wall-clock time)".

examples.source: Ask your administrator to contact IBM support if you need a different interactive TTL or system maximum TTL.
examples.translation: Minta administratormu untuk menghubungi dukungan IBM jika kamu membutuhkan interactive TTL atau TTL maksimum sistem yang berbeda.
examples.suggested: Minta administrator Anda untuk menghubungi dukungan IBM jika Anda membutuhkan interactive TTL atau TTL maksimum sistem yang berbeda.
examples.why: This sentence switches from 'Anda' to '-mu' and 'kamu', even though the earlier sentences of the entry and the rest of the page use 'Anda'.

examples.source: usage is the wall clock time the QPU is **committed to the session**
examples.translation: penggunaan adalah waktu jam dinding selama QPU **didedikasikan untuk Session**
examples.suggested: penggunaan adalah waktu nyata (wall-clock time) selama QPU **didedikasikan untuk Session**
examples.why: 'Waktu jam dinding' is a literal calque. Indonesian technical writing usually says 'waktu nyata' or keeps the English term in parentheses. The meaning is still recognizable.

editor_note: All four rewritten entries (9, 13, 28, 37) say what the English says. The reasoning in entry 13 that equal gate times make error rates "sebanding", with its relaxation caveat, is intact, and so is the "persyaratan ini" logic in entry 28. Two phrasings are stiff. In entry 9, "mengurangi ... hingga dua kali lipat" copies the English "reduce by a factor of two" word for word, and "hingga setengahnya" says it more clearly. In entry 28, "errornya lebih tertekan" for "error-suppressed" sounds robotic and should become "sehingga error-nya lebih rendah". Entry 37 ("Contoh:") is fine.

examples.source: can reduce the duration and error for single-qubit rotations of arbitrary angle by up to a factor of two
examples.translation: dapat mengurangi durasi dan error untuk rotasi satu-Qubit dengan sudut sembarang hingga dua kali lipat
examples.suggested: dapat memangkas durasi dan error rotasi satu-Qubit dengan sudut sembarang hingga setengahnya
examples.why: 'Mengurangi ... dua kali lipat' copies the English phrase literally and reads oddly, because 'dua kali lipat' usually means doubling. 'Hingga setengahnya' makes the reduction unmistakable.

examples.source: create a more efficient (and thus error-suppressed) quantum circuit
examples.translation: menciptakan Circuit kuantum yang lebih efisien (dan dengan demikian errornya lebih tertekan)
examples.suggested: menghasilkan Circuit kuantum yang lebih efisien (sehingga error-nya lebih rendah)
examples.why: 'Dengan demikian errornya lebih tertekan' is stiff, word-for-word phrasing. A native technical writer would use 'sehingga' and 'lebih rendah'.

editor_note: None of the 10 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The units caveat in [92] (nanodetik vs detik), the init-error vs prob_meas1_prep0 distinction in [96], and the "error = 1" caveat in [106] ("dianggap tidak terdefinisi", "kamu harus berhati-hati") are all faithful. There are three small editorial slips. [60] splits the UI label as "Bagian data Calibration" while [70], [95] and [97] use "Bagian Calibration data". [101] leaves the English "or" in the accordion title "CLOPS (or CLOPS_h)". [96] renders "subtly different" as "sedikit berbeda" ("slightly different"), which loses the sense of a fine but real distinction.

examples.line_approx: Calibration data section: Qubit dropdown menu
examples.source: Calibration data section: Qubit dropdown menu; find the *$T_1$ median* value in the Details section
examples.translation: Bagian data Calibration: menu dropdown Qubit; temukan nilai *median $T_1$* di bagian Details
examples.suggested: Bagian Calibration data: menu dropdown Qubit; temukan nilai *median $T_1$* di bagian Details
examples.why: "Calibration data" is the name of a UI section, so it should stay intact. The file writes "Bagian Calibration data" everywhere else, and splitting it here makes the label harder to spot on the platform.

examples.source: <AccordionItem title="CLOPS (or CLOPS_h)">
examples.translation: <AccordionItem title="CLOPS (or CLOPS_h)">
examples.suggested: <AccordionItem title="CLOPS (atau CLOPS_h)">
examples.why: The English conjunction "or" was left untranslated in a visible heading.

examples.line_approx: Note that this is subtly different than the quantity
examples.source: Note that this is subtly different than the quantity [`prob_meas1_prep0`]
examples.translation: Perhatikan bahwa ini sedikit berbeda dari kuantitas [`prob_meas1_prep0`]
examples.suggested: Perhatikan bahwa ini berbeda secara halus dari kuantitas [`prob_meas1_prep0`]
examples.why: "Subtly" means a fine but real conceptual distinction, while "sedikit" suggests a small numerical gap. This is a minor shift in nuance and does not mislead.

editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries (15, 24, 25, 36, 45) misleads a learner. Their meaning matches the English, including the "can always flip a gate's direction" and "can always be represented ... by introducing SWAP gates" claims in [25] and the causal "because this layout respects the circuit's connectivity" in [36]. One real consistency slip: the heading in [24] reads "Peta coupling", but the paragraph right below it in [25], and every other entry on the page ([0], [23], [26]), uses "coupling map". A reader sees two names for one concept side by side. There is also a small naturalness nit in [25]: "di antara mereka" uses a personal pronoun for qubits, and "di antaranya" would read more natively.

examples.source: Coupling map {#coupling-map}
examples.translation: Peta coupling {#coupling-map}
examples.suggested: Coupling map {#coupling-map}
examples.why: The section body ([25]) and the rest of the page keep 'coupling map'. The half-translated heading 'Peta coupling' introduces a second name for the same concept right above its definition.

examples.source: which qubits are connected and hence have two-qubit gates between them
examples.translation: qubit mana yang terhubung dan karenanya memiliki Gate dua qubit di antara mereka
examples.suggested: qubit mana yang saling terhubung sehingga dapat dikenai gate dua qubit di antaranya
examples.why: 'mereka' is a personal pronoun and sounds calqued when it refers to qubits. 'di antaranya' is the natural Indonesian choice for inanimate referents.

editor_note: All four rewritten entries (3, 9, 15, 17) keep the English meaning. Every negation survives, including "IBM tidak bertanggung jawab atas pencadangan…", and so do the caveats "sesuai kebutuhan" and "jika tersedia". The problems are wording that a native editor would smooth. In entry 15, "regulated data" is calqued as "data yang diatur" and "data in motion" is rendered literally as "data dalam perjalanan", where "data yang tunduk pada regulasi" and "data saat transit" are the usual terms. Entry 17 has the slash gloss "penyediaan/provisioning", and entry 9 has the stiff "Menyediakan ketersediaan" plus the bare noun "Migrasi" in a column where the other cells use imperatives.

examples.source: Ensure that personal and regulated data is not provided.
examples.translation: Pastikan bahwa data pribadi dan data yang diatur tidak diberikan.
examples.suggested: Pastikan bahwa data pribadi dan data yang tunduk pada regulasi tidak diberikan.
examples.why: 'data yang diatur' is a literal calque and unclear to a reader. 'Regulated data' means data that is subject to regulation.

examples.source: Encryption methods such as HTTPS and TLS are used to protect data in motion.
examples.translation: …digunakan untuk melindungi data dalam perjalanan.
examples.suggested: …digunakan untuk melindungi data saat transit.
examples.why: 'data dalam perjalanan' is a word-for-word calque. Indonesian security writing normally says 'data saat transit' or 'data in transit'.

examples.source: Restore or rebuild the provisioning environments and resources in the affected regions.
examples.translation: Memulihkan atau membangun kembali lingkungan penyediaan/provisioning dan sumber daya…
examples.suggested: Memulihkan atau membangun kembali lingkungan provisioning dan sumber daya…
examples.why: The slash gloss reads like a translator's note left in the text. Choose one rendering.

examples.source: Migrate to a supported version before end-of-support for an old version.
examples.translation: Migrasi ke versi yang didukung sebelum akhir dukungan untuk versi lama.
examples.suggested: Lakukan migrasi ke versi yang didukung sebelum dukungan untuk versi lama berakhir.
examples.why: The bare noun 'Migrasi' does not match the imperative form used elsewhere in the 'Tanggung jawabmu' column. 'akhir dukungan untuk' is also stiff.

editor_note: The four rewritten entries (2, 4, 5, 6) keep the meaning, and nothing in them would mislead a learner. The problems are all in entry 6. Its opening "ada lebih banyak hal dalam memahami ... daripada sekadar menyadari" copies the English "there is more to X than" structure word for word, which reads as translationese. "Memahami dengan tepat bagaimana caranya" misreads "exactly how" as "the way to do it", when it means how the measurement affects the unmeasured systems. Entry 6 also uses the non-standard spelling "mempengaruhi"; the standard KBBI form is "memengaruhi".

examples.source: There is, however, more to understanding multiple quantum systems than simply recognizing that they may be viewed collectively as single systems.
examples.translation: Namun, ada lebih banyak hal dalam memahami sistem kuantum majemuk daripada sekadar menyadari bahwa sistem-sistem tersebut dapat dipandang secara kolektif sebagai satu sistem tunggal.
examples.suggested: Namun, memahami sistem kuantum majemuk tidak cukup hanya dengan menyadari bahwa sistem-sistem tersebut dapat dipandang secara kolektif sebagai satu sistem tunggal.
examples.why: This copies the English 'there is more to X than Y' structure word for word. An Indonesian technical writer would say it is 'not enough just to...'.

examples.source: In general, this will affect the state of the systems that were not measured, and it is important to understand exactly how when analyzing quantum algorithms and protocols.
examples.translation: Secara umum, ini akan mempengaruhi keadaan sistem yang tidak diukur, dan penting untuk memahami dengan tepat bagaimana caranya saat menganalisis algoritma dan protokol kuantum.
examples.suggested: Secara umum, hal ini akan memengaruhi keadaan sistem yang tidak diukur, dan penting untuk memahami bagaimana tepatnya pengaruh itu terjadi saat menganalisis algoritma dan protokol kuantum.
examples.why: 'bagaimana caranya' means 'the way to do it', but the source means how the effect happens. The standard KBBI spelling is 'memengaruhi', not 'mempengaruhi'.

editor_note: The four rewritten entries (12, 16, 21, 22) keep the meaning of the English: nothing is inverted, no caveat is dropped, and the physics is intact. What a native editor would still fix is calqued phrasing. In [12], "Tidak ada yang menyarankan sebaliknya!" copies "Nobody suggests otherwise!" word for word, and "Yang mungkin lebih sering terjadi, ada kesalahan…" drops the hedge "could". In [21], "Daripada bertindak" and the hybrid "meng-encode-nya" read like translationese, and in [22], "Sangat penting bahwa ini dilakukan baik secara sering maupun secara paralel" is stiff. The non-standard "mempengaruhi" (standard form: "memengaruhi") also appears.

examples.source: Perhaps more likely, there could be errors that are localized ... Nobody suggests otherwise!
examples.translation: Yang mungkin lebih sering terjadi, ada kesalahan yang terlokalisir tetapi tetap mempengaruhi ... Tidak ada yang menyarankan sebaliknya!
examples.suggested: Yang mungkin lebih sering terjadi, bisa saja ada kesalahan yang terlokalisasi tetapi tetap memengaruhi ... Tidak ada yang membantah hal itu!
examples.why: The literal rendering of 'Nobody suggests otherwise!' is a calque with unclear meaning. The hedge 'could' is dropped. 'mempengaruhi' and 'terlokalisir' are non-standard (standard forms: 'memengaruhi', 'terlokalisasi').

examples.source: Rather than acting directly on these logical qubits, the gadgets act on the *physical* qubits that encode them.
examples.translation: Daripada bertindak langsung pada qubit logis ini, gadget bertindak pada qubit *fisik* yang meng-encode-nya.
examples.suggested: Alih-alih bertindak langsung pada qubit logis ini, gadget bertindak pada qubit *fisik* yang mengodekannya.
examples.why: 'Daripada' at the start of a sentence is a calque of 'Rather than'. 'meng-encode-nya' is an English/Indonesian hybrid, and 'mengodekannya' is the standard verb.

examples.source: It is critically important that this is done both frequently and in parallel.
examples.translation: Sangat penting bahwa ini dilakukan baik secara sering maupun secara paralel.
examples.suggested: Sangat penting agar koreksi ini dilakukan sesering mungkin dan secara paralel.
examples.why: 'Sangat penting bahwa' plus 'baik secara sering maupun' copies the English syntax. It reads stiffly, though the meaning is correct.

editor_note: The three rewritten entries (2-4) keep the English meaning: the codes "hanya mampu menoleransi tingkat kesalahan yang sangat rendah", the newer codes tolerate "jauh lebih tinggi" error rates, and CSS combines *pasangan* of classical codes. Nothing here would mislead a learner. The remaining problems are phrasing. Entry 3's "menengok sekilas untuk pertama kalinya" is a stiff calque of "take a first look". Entry 4's "mengambil *pasangan* tertentu kode" drops the "dari", and "dinamai dari" is less idiomatic than "dinamai menurut". In entry 2, "mendalami" ("study in depth") slightly overstates "begin an exploration".

examples.source: we'll take a first look at some more sophisticated quantum error correcting code constructions
examples.translation: kita akan menengok sekilas untuk pertama kalinya beberapa konstruksi kode koreksi kesalahan kuantum yang lebih canggih
examples.suggested: kita akan mulai berkenalan dengan beberapa konstruksi kode koreksi kesalahan kuantum yang lebih canggih
examples.why: 'menengok sekilas untuk pertama kalinya' is a word-for-word calque and reads awkwardly. A native writer would say 'mulai berkenalan dengan' or 'melihat sekilas'.

examples.source: named for Robert Calderbank, Peter Shor, and Andrew Steane ... take certain *pairs* of classical error correcting codes
examples.translation: dinamai dari Robert Calderbank, ... mengambil *pasangan* tertentu kode koreksi kesalahan klasik
examples.suggested: dinamai menurut Robert Calderbank, ... mengambil *pasangan-pasangan* tertentu dari kode koreksi kesalahan klasik
examples.why: 'dinamai menurut' is the standard collocation. The phrase 'pasangan tertentu kode' needs 'dari', and the plural makes clear the construction applies to many possible pairs.

examples.source: represent a natural place to begin an exploration of quantum error correction
examples.translation: merupakan titik awal yang wajar untuk mendalami koreksi kesalahan kuantum
examples.suggested: merupakan titik awal yang wajar untuk mulai menjelajahi koreksi kesalahan kuantum
examples.why: 'mendalami' means to study in depth, which slightly strengthens 'begin an exploration'. 'mulai menjelajahi' keeps the introductory sense.

editor_note: Entry 70 keeps the meaning of both parts. In (a), the classical bit is limited to 0 or 1 and the qubit is in superposition. In (b), CLOPS is defined as sequential operations per second, including some classical interfacing such as loading parameters from the circuit ("rangkaian"). The one slip is terminology: "the state 0 or 1" becomes "keadaan 0 atau 1", but the rest of the page uses "state" for this idea (for example "state kuantum" and "ruang state" in entry 59). A learner won't be misled, but the term should be aligned with the rest of the file.

examples.source: which can only adopt the state 0 or 1
examples.translation: yang hanya bisa berada dalam keadaan 0 atau 1
examples.suggested: yang hanya bisa berada dalam state 0 atau 1
examples.why: The rest of the page consistently renders 'state' as 'state' (entry 59: 'state kuantum', 'ruang state'). Using 'keadaan' only here breaks that convention. The meaning is unchanged, so this is minor.

editor_note: All three rewritten entries (13–15) keep the English meaning and none would mislead a learner. There are three small problems. The new heading [13] translates the term as "Kesiapan kuantum", but the definition directly below it [14] bolds the English "Quantum readiness" with no gloss, and the rest of the page keeps the English term. The heading and the term it introduces should be tied together. In [14], "Ini mengkarakterisasi" is a stiff calque of "It characterizes". Also, "quantum-savvy" becomes "paham kuantum" in [14] but "melek kuantum" in [25], which translates the same phrase.

examples.source: **Quantum readiness** is a continuously evolving measure of organizational proficiency...
examples.translation: **Quantum readiness** adalah ukuran yang terus berkembang dari kemahiran organisasi...
examples.suggested: **Quantum readiness** (kesiapan kuantum) adalah ukuran yang terus berkembang dari kemahiran organisasi...
examples.why: The heading [13] now reads 'Kesiapan kuantum', but the definition just below it bolds the English term with no gloss. A short parenthetical ties the heading to the term the rest of the page uses.

examples.source: It characterizes the company’s progressive capabilities to leverage quantum technology...
examples.translation: Ini mengkarakterisasi kemampuan progresif perusahaan untuk memanfaatkan teknologi kuantum...
examples.suggested: Konsep ini menggambarkan kemampuan perusahaan yang terus bertumbuh untuk memanfaatkan teknologi kuantum...
examples.why: 'mengkarakterisasi' is a direct calque. An Indonesian business or technical writer would use 'menggambarkan' and an explicit subject rather than a bare 'Ini'.

examples.source: respond to threats from quantum-savvy competitors
examples.translation: merespons ancaman dari pesaing yang paham kuantum
examples.suggested: merespons ancaman dari pesaing yang melek kuantum
examples.why: Entry [25] translates the same phrase as 'pesaing yang melek kuantum'. Pick one rendering for the whole file.

editor_note: Entry 9 keeps the English meaning: the exam is optional ("jika kamu mau"), it follows the course, and the badge comes only after passing. The one flaw is the closing "lencana IBM Quantum Business Foundations milikmu", which copies the English "your" word for word. A native Indonesian editor would drop "milikmu" because "mendapatkan" already shows who gets the badge. "Ujian lencana" for "badging exam" and "membuka tautan" for "follow the link" are acceptable choices.

examples.source: Upon passing the badging exam you will earn your IBM Quantum Business Foundations badge.
examples.translation: Setelah lulus ujian lencana, kamu akan mendapatkan lencana IBM Quantum Business Foundations milikmu.
examples.suggested: Setelah lulus ujian lencana, kamu akan mendapatkan lencana IBM Quantum Business Foundations.
examples.why: The trailing 'milikmu' copies the English 'your' and is redundant in Indonesian because 'mendapatkan' already shows who receives the badge. Removing it reads more naturally, and the meaning is unchanged.

editor_note: The meaning holds up throughout. The distinctions between suppression, mitigation and detection/correction, the "limited form of error correction" caveat in [7] and the noise-tailoring point in [8] all come through accurately. Two small wording slips are worth fixing. In [9], "steadily coming within reach" became "perlahan mulai terjangkau" ("slowly"), which shifts the tone from steady progress to slowness. In [11], "Yuk ikuti kita" uses the inclusive "kita" where the exclusive "kami" is needed ("join us"), and "mewujudkan" slightly overstates "bring within reach".

examples.source: increasingly advanced forms of error correction are steadily coming within reach
examples.translation: bentuk-bentuk error correction yang semakin canggih perlahan mulai terjangkau
examples.suggested: bentuk-bentuk error correction yang semakin canggih kian mendekati jangkauan
examples.why: 'perlahan' means 'slowly', which turns the positive 'steadily' into a hint of slowness.

examples.source: Join us as we explore the tools that will help bring quantum advantage within reach.
examples.translation: Yuk ikuti kita menjelajahi tools yang akan membantu mewujudkan quantum advantage.
examples.suggested: Yuk, bergabunglah bersama kami menjelajahi tools yang akan membantu membawa quantum advantage semakin dekat.
examples.why: 'ikuti kita' uses the inclusive 'we', but the reader is being asked to join the authors, so the exclusive 'kami' is correct. 'mewujudkan' (to achieve) also claims more than 'bring within reach'.

editor_note: All five rewritten entries are faithful: equal superposition is "superposisi seragam" in both [23] and [35], "inversion about the average amplitude" is "inversi terhadap amplitudo rata-rata", the "sekitar $\sqrt{N}$ kali" hedge from the English is kept, and "Pascapemrosesan hasil" is correct in [41] and [49].

The course titles are translated faithfully and read naturally, for example "Desain Algoritma Variasional", "Komputasi Kuantum Skala Utilitas" and "Kimia Kuantum dengan VQE". Keeping the loanwords "Error", "Tools" and "Machine Learning" is a defensible convention.

None of the 11 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entries 9, 25, 50 and 174 keep the quadratic-speedup caveats and the reflection logic intact. In entry 104, "by far" became "sejauh ini", which means "so far". The next clause ("setidaknya satu orde besaran lebih tinggi") still gives the margin, but the phrase should read "dengan selisih jauh". Entry 63 renders "circular" as "berputar-putar", which reads as "beating around the bush" rather than circular logic, and turns "broadly useful" into "sangat berguna". Entries 66 and 39 carry calques ("Dengan ide-ide ini dalam pikiran", "berharap untuk bekerja secara substansial").

examples.source: with the highest probability by far
examples.translation: dengan probabilitas tertinggi sejauh ini
examples.suggested: dengan probabilitas tertinggi, jauh melampaui yang lain
examples.why: 'sejauh ini' means 'so far' (temporal). That misreads 'by far' and weakens the emphasis, although the next clause about an order of magnitude keeps the claim.

examples.source: Amplitude amplification is a broadly useful subroutine. Even if this first demonstration seems circular
examples.translation: Amplifikasi amplitudo adalah subrutin yang sangat berguna. Meskipun demonstrasi pertama ini terkesan berputar-putar
examples.suggested: Amplifikasi amplitudo adalah subrutin yang berguna secara luas. Meskipun demonstrasi pertama ini terkesan seperti logika melingkar
examples.why: 'Berputar-putar' suggests long-winded or evasive, not circular reasoning (needing to know the answer to build the oracle). 'Sangat berguna' also drops the sense of 'broadly', meaning widely applicable.

examples.source: With these ideas in mind, ... rather than from knowledge of the answer.
examples.translation: Dengan ide-ide ini dalam pikiran, ... daripada dari pengetahuan jawaban.
examples.suggested: Berbekal ide-ide ini, ... bukan dari jawaban yang sudah diketahui.
examples.why: This is a word-for-word calque of an English idiom, and the closing phrase is stiff.

examples.source: for those who hope to work substantially with quantum computers
examples.translation: bagi mereka yang berharap untuk bekerja secara substansial dengan komputer kuantum
examples.suggested: bagi yang ingin banyak bekerja dengan komputer kuantum
examples.why: 'Bekerja secara substansial' is translationese. A native technical writer would not phrase it this way.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning and read naturally: entry 6 renders "answer keys" as "kunci jawaban" and "quick survey" as "survei singkat", and entry 9 renders "should be sufficient" as "matriks $2 \times 2$ sudah cukup".

The 20 rewritten entries keep their meaning: the faster-than-light caveat (25), the ~95%/~5% noise figures (105), the conditional X/Z timing in qubit 12 (111), and the "more gates, more errors" lesson (119, 128) all match the English. What remains is small editorial polish. [139] turns "heads twice in a row" into "the same side twice", which still makes the finite-sampling point but is a different event. [94] uses "primitive" where [81] uses "primitif", and [123] spells "mempengaruhi" where [15] has the standard "memengaruhi". [107] ("komunikasi klasik gate tambahan") and [66] ("Dua teman", "peringatan" for caveats, "a lot" dropped) read stiffly.

examples.source: just as flipping a coin might yield heads twice in a row
examples.translation: seperti melempar koin yang bisa jatuh pada sisi yang sama dua kali berturut-turut
examples.suggested: seperti melempar koin yang bisa menghasilkan sisi angka dua kali berturut-turut
examples.why: The example changes from 'heads twice' to 'same side twice', which is a different and more likely event. The finite-sampling point still holds, so this is minor.

examples.source: A "Sampler" is a primitive designed to sample possible states
examples.translation: "Sampler" adalah primitive yang dirancang untuk mengambil sampel
examples.suggested: "Sampler" adalah primitif yang dirancang untuk mengambil sampel
examples.why: Entry 81 renders 'primitives' as 'primitif'. Here the English form is left untranslated, so the file uses two spellings.

examples.source: (though the classical communication of extra gates is not instant)
examples.translation: (meskipun komunikasi klasik gate tambahan tidak instan)
examples.suggested: (meskipun komunikasi klasik tentang gate tambahan yang perlu diterapkan tidak instan)
examples.why: The noun-stack calque drops the relation between the two nouns. 'tentang' makes clear that the message is about which gates to apply.

examples.source: The two friends move their qubits ... This comes with a lot of caveats ... when we move quantum information around a lot.
examples.translation: Dua teman memindahkan qubit mereka ... Ini disertai banyak peringatan ... ketika memindahkan informasi kuantum ke mana-mana.
examples.suggested: Kedua teman itu memindahkan qubit mereka ... Ini disertai banyak catatan/kendala ... ketika sering memindahkan informasi kuantum.
examples.why: 'Kedua' is the natural determiner here, and 'catatan' or 'kendala' fits 'caveat' better than 'peringatan'. The translation also drops 'a lot', which ties the errors to frequent movement.

examples.source: a measurement of one qubit affects or even determines
examples.translation: pengukuran satu qubit mempengaruhi atau bahkan menentukan
examples.suggested: pengukuran satu qubit memengaruhi atau bahkan menentukan
examples.why: KBBI's standard form is 'memengaruhi', which entry 15 already uses, so the spelling is inconsistent within the file.

editor_note: None of the 9 rewritten entries changes the meaning. Entries 14, 87, 155, 156, 165, 209 and 260 are faithful, and the caveats and quantities are all kept, including the 0.735 Å distance, "tidak dapat ditangani" for intractable and the noise and depth caveats in 209. The problems are in entries 207 and 173. Entry 207 has a calque ("kita belajar bahwa diperlukan untuk mendapatkan"), leaves "trial quantum states" in English even though the page elsewhere uses "keadaan kuantum trial", and uses both "sirkuit" and "Circuit" in the same sentence. Entry 173 calls the check-in problem "soal pemeriksaan", while the rest of the page uses "pertanyaan check-in".

examples.source: we learned that it is necessary to obtain the appropriate molecular Hamiltonian
examples.translation: kita belajar bahwa diperlukan untuk mendapatkan Hamiltonian molekuler yang sesuai
examples.suggested: kita belajar bahwa kita perlu mendapatkan Hamiltonian molekuler yang sesuai
examples.why: A calque of 'it is necessary to'. 'bahwa diperlukan untuk' has no subject and reads as machine-translated.

examples.source: to prepare trial quantum states within VQE ... appropriate ansatz circuit structure
examples.translation: untuk menyiapkan trial quantum states dalam VQE, ... struktur Circuit ansatz yang tepat
examples.suggested: untuk menyiapkan keadaan kuantum trial dalam VQE, ... struktur sirkuit ansatz yang tepat
examples.why: An English phrase is left untranslated even though entry 84 renders it as 'keadaan kuantum trial', and 'sirkuit' and 'Circuit' both appear in the same sentence.

examples.source: we will actually calculate this value in the check-in problem
examples.translation: kita akan benar-benar menghitung nilai ini pada soal pemeriksaan
examples.suggested: kita akan menghitung nilai ini secara langsung pada pertanyaan check-in
examples.why: Entries 70, 96 and 177 call it 'pertanyaan check-in'. 'soal pemeriksaan' doesn't match and hides the link to the check-in section.

editor_note: Rewritten entry 26 is faithful: it keeps "bukan sekadar tidak diketahui, tetapi tidak terdefinisi secara fisik", the ±z collapse ("meruntuhkan", matching entry 12) and "tepat berlawanan dengan spin positron", and renders "less-dramatically" as the defensible "dengan lebih lugas sebagai \"fisika non-lokal\"".

The translation is faithful throughout. The hard technical passages come through correctly: the little-endian convention, the CNOT |BA⟩ ordering, the Toffoli-as-AND explanation and the reversible gates, where "tidak dapat dibalik" is used for AND/OR. The one real wording problem is in the challenge question [240]. "equal superposition" became "superposisi yang sama", which most naturally reads as "the same superposition" rather than an equal-weight one, so it should say "superposisi seimbang" or "superposisi dengan bobot sama". The rest are consistency slips. Entanglement is "Entanglement" in most places but "Keterjeratan" in [226]. "computational basis states" is "keadaan basis komputasi" in most places but left as "basis state" / "computational basis" in [124]/[125]. The heading is "Uji pemahamanmu" once in [133] and "Cek pemahamanmu" everywhere else. [174] has a clumsy opening clause.

examples.source: prepare each qubit in an equal superposition of 0 and 1
examples.translation: mempersiapkan setiap qubit dalam superposisi yang sama dari 0 dan 1
examples.suggested: mempersiapkan setiap qubit dalam superposisi seimbang (bobot sama) dari 0 dan 1
examples.why: 'yang sama' reads as 'the same superposition', not an equal-amplitude one, which weakens the instruction the learner has to follow.

examples.source: Entanglement means the state of one qubit is independent...
examples.translation: Keterjeratan berarti keadaan satu qubit tidak bergantung...
examples.suggested: Entanglement berarti keadaan satu qubit tidak bergantung...
examples.why: Every other entry, including the section heading [73] and [77], keeps 'Entanglement'. This is the only place it becomes 'Keterjeratan'.

examples.source: For computational basis values $a,b\in\{0,1\}$
examples.translation: Untuk nilai computational basis $a,b\in\{0,1\}$
examples.suggested: Untuk nilai basis komputasi $a,b\in\{0,1\}$
examples.why: The rest of the file uses 'basis komputasi' / 'keadaan basis komputasi'. Entry [124] likewise leaves 'basis state' in English.

examples.source: First, remembering that quantum gates are *reversible*, we cannot simply overwrite the inputs.
examples.translation: Pertama, ingat bahwa Gate kuantum bersifat *reversibel*, kita tidak bisa begitu saja menimpa input-nya.
examples.suggested: Pertama, karena gate kuantum bersifat *reversibel*, kita tidak bisa begitu saja menimpa input-nya.
examples.why: The 'ingat bahwa ..., kita ...' construction is run-on and calqued from the English. A causal 'karena' reads naturally.

examples.source: Check your understanding
examples.translation: Uji pemahamanmu
examples.suggested: Cek pemahamanmu
examples.why: The other eight instances of this recurring heading use 'Cek pemahamanmu'.

editor_note: The three rewritten entries are faithful and natural: "kunci jawaban dan panduan penempatan dalam kurikulum umum" keeps both deliverables, "matriks $2 \times 2$ sudah cukup" keeps the sufficiency claim, and "bisa langsung dijalankan apa adanya" keeps the caveat about Python.

None of the five rewritten entries (21, 22, 128, 134, 143) changes the meaning in a way that would mislead a learner. The 50/50 claim, the "superposition is not a coin flip" point, the Bloch-sphere polar/azimuthal mapping ("sudut polar θ", "sudut azimut φ") and the pointer to the Ketaksamaan Bell module all match the English. Two phrasings are stiff and follow English word order. In entry 22 the two halves of the 50/50 statement are word-ordered differently ("peluang 50% ... 50% peluang"). In entry 21, "ada lebih banyak hal di dalamnya" is a literal rendering of "much more to it than that".

examples.source: there will be a 50% chance we measure $|0\rangle$, 50% chance we measure $|1\rangle$
examples.translation: akan ada peluang 50% kita mengukur $|0\rangle$, 50% peluang kita mengukur $|1\rangle$
examples.suggested: peluang kita mengukur $|0\rangle$ adalah 50%, dan peluang mengukur $|1\rangle$ juga 50%
examples.why: The two halves of the parallel statement use different word orders, and the flow follows English syntax. A native writer would keep them parallel.

examples.source: we will soon see that there is much more to it than that
examples.translation: kita akan segera melihat bahwa ada lebih banyak hal di dalamnya
examples.suggested: kita akan segera melihat bahwa sebenarnya jauh lebih dari itu
examples.why: This is a literal calque of the English idiom. It reads stiffly, though the meaning is preserved.

editor_note: The three rewritten entries are faithful: [2] keeps "empat qubit … eksperimen dua qubit" and "nilai ekspektasi" intact, [5] keeps "Petakan Hamiltonian", and [31] glosses "fake backend (backend tiruan)" and keeps the "mode lokal (yaitu, pada simulator lokal)" caveat.

Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning. Entry 34 is accurate: "Kedalamannya berkurang lebih dari setengahnya" and "circuit yang lebih dalam" both match the source. The only problem is in entry 2, where "otherwise" is calqued as "yang jika tidak demikian akan disisipkan oleh proses routing". This reads stiffly, and "tidak demikian" has no clear referent. A native editor would say directly what happens without the cut, as in the suggestion below.

examples.source: avoiding the swap gates that would otherwise be introduced by routing
examples.translation: sehingga menghindari swap gate yang jika tidak demikian akan disisipkan oleh proses routing
examples.suggested: sehingga terhindar dari swap gate yang seharusnya disisipkan oleh proses routing jika Gate tersebut tidak dipotong
examples.why: "jika tidak demikian" is a word-for-word calque of "otherwise". It is stiff and its referent is vague. Saying the condition outright (if the gate is not cut) reads natively and teaches the same point more clearly.

editor_note: Entry 4 is faithful and reads naturally: "paket ekstensi resmi yang menyediakan algoritma dan teknik komputasi kuantum khusus" keeps "official" and "specialized", and "dilengkapi tutorial dengan kode yang bisa dijalankan" is an idiomatic way to say "includes tutorials with executable code".

Neither rewritten entry changes the meaning, so nothing here would mislead a learner. Entry 38 uses two words for the same boxing concept within one paragraph: "sirkuit yang sudah di-box" and then "sirkuit tanpa kotak" for "non-boxed circuit". It should use one term, e.g. "sirkuit yang tidak di-box". In entry 16, "Jadikan box semua lapisan gate 2q" is a stiff calque of the English verb "Box". "Bungkus semua lapisan gate 2q ... ke dalam box" reads more naturally. The "left-dressed" gloss is fine.

examples.source: One can also pass a non-boxed circuit containing ``PauliLindbladError`` instructions
examples.translation: Kita juga bisa memberikan sirkuit tanpa kotak yang berisi instruksi ``PauliLindbladError``
examples.suggested: Kita juga bisa memberikan sirkuit yang tidak di-box yang berisi instruksi ``PauliLindbladError``
examples.why: The previous sentence says 'di-box' for the same concept. Switching to 'tanpa kotak' breaks the boxed/non-boxed contrast inside one paragraph.

examples.source: Box all 2q gate layers and terminal measurements.
examples.translation: Jadikan box semua lapisan gate 2q dan pengukuran terminal.
examples.suggested: Bungkus semua lapisan gate 2q dan pengukuran terminal ke dalam box.
examples.why: 'Jadikan box' is a literal calque of the English verb 'box'. The meaning comes through, but it reads stiffly.

editor_note: None of the 10 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The claims (native interactions, parameters assigned before transpilation, the fractional version being more compact, RX-only keeping the standard workflow) and the caveats "(dalam batas tertentu)" and "berpotensi meningkatkan performa" all match the English. Entry 95 has a clumsy mixed gloss: "metode translation (translasi basis) `constructor-beta`" should just say "translasi basis". Entry 59 leaves out "those from", so the sentence compares the metrics to the standard workflow itself rather than to that workflow's metrics.

examples.source: we apply the transpiler using `constructor-beta` translation provided by the `qiskit-basis-constructor` package
examples.translation: kita menerapkan Transpiler menggunakan metode translation (translasi basis) `constructor-beta` yang disediakan oleh paket
examples.suggested: kita menjalankan transpiler dengan metode translasi basis `constructor-beta` dari paket `qiskit-basis-constructor`
examples.why: The English word 'translation' followed by an Indonesian gloss in parentheses reads like a note left in the text. The gloss by itself is enough and reads naturally.

examples.source: compare these metrics to those from a standard workflow later
examples.translation: membandingkan metrik-metrik ini dengan alur kerja standar nanti
examples.suggested: nanti membandingkan metrik-metrik ini dengan metrik dari alur kerja standar
examples.why: 'those from' is missing, so the metrics are compared to the workflow instead of to its metrics. Putting 'nanti' at the end also sounds stiff.

editor_note: I found no meaning errors. The implicit-versus-explicit solvent trade-off in [11], the CASCI comparison in [12]/[33] and the combined execute/post-process loop in [43] all match the English. Entry [13] reads like a different translator wrote it: it keeps "solvent" in English ("model solvent implisit") where the rest of the page uses "pelarut", and it uses "workflow" and "kalkulasi" where the rest of the page uses "alur kerja" and "perhitungan". It also leaves "sustainability" in English with a gloss in parentheses. In [14], "some advantage" became plain "keuntungan", which makes the claim a little stronger than the English.

examples.source: Understanding how solvents affect molecular properties is relevant to sustainability research ... introduces a workflow for combining quantum electronic-structure calculations with an implicit solvent model
examples.translation: Memahami bagaimana solvent memengaruhi properti molekul relevan dengan penelitian sustainability (keberlanjutan) ... memperkenalkan workflow untuk menggabungkan kalkulasi struktur elektronik kuantum dengan model solvent implisit
examples.suggested: Memahami bagaimana pelarut memengaruhi sifat molekul relevan dengan penelitian keberlanjutan ... memperkenalkan alur kerja untuk menggabungkan perhitungan struktur elektronik kuantum dengan model pelarut implisit
examples.why: The rest of the file uses pelarut, alur kerja and perhitungan (see [0], [11], [6], [18]). This entry switches to English or loan words, which is inconsistent and reads unevenly.

examples.source: Users also gain some advantage in parallel processing of programs
examples.translation: Pengguna juga mendapatkan keuntungan dalam pemrosesan paralel program
examples.suggested: Pengguna juga mendapatkan sejumlah keuntungan dalam pemrosesan paralel program
examples.why: Leaving out the hedge 'some' makes the claim slightly stronger than the source.

examples.source: Sample-based quantum diagonalization
examples.translation: Sample-based quantum diagonalization
examples.suggested: Diagonalisasi kuantum berbasis sampel
examples.why: Entry [9] translates this same phrase as 'Diagonalisasi kuantum berbasis sampel', but here it stays in English. This inconsistency is minor.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The 1→Region A / 0→Region B mapping, the d_i/2 target and the transpile_only caveat all come through correctly, and the register is a consistent "Anda". I found three things an editor would still change. In [21], "pelanggaran kendala kuadrat" reads as "violation of the quadratic constraint", but the source means the violation is squared, so it should be "kuadrat pelanggaran kendala". In [23], "Memperluas" is a calque of algebraic "expanding" and should be "Menjabarkan". In [53], "market" is left in English, although "pasar" is used for the same concept everywhere else in the file.

examples.source: minimize the squared constraint violation (the cost function)
examples.translation: meminimalkan pelanggaran kendala kuadrat (fungsi biaya)
examples.suggested: meminimalkan kuadrat pelanggaran kendala (fungsi biaya)
examples.why: The word order makes "kuadrat" modify "kendala" (a quadratic constraint) instead of the violation being squared. The formula right beside it makes the intent clear, but the prose is ambiguous.

examples.source: Expanding this gives a form that is equivalent to a QUBO problem.
examples.translation: Memperluas ini menghasilkan bentuk yang setara dengan masalah ...
examples.suggested: Menjabarkan persamaan ini menghasilkan bentuk yang setara dengan masalah ...
examples.why: "Memperluas" means to broaden or enlarge. For expanding an algebraic expression the usual Indonesian word is "menjabarkan".

examples.source: partition markets into two separate regions ... assigns that specific market to Region A
examples.translation: membagi market menjadi dua wilayah terpisah ... market tertentu ke Wilayah A
examples.suggested: membagi pasar menjadi dua wilayah terpisah ... pasar tertentu ke Wilayah A
examples.why: Entries [13], [14], [16] and [17] consistently use "pasar" for these markets. Here it switches to the English "market", which is inconsistent within the file.

editor_note: Entries 21 and 26 are faithful and read naturally. Entry 57 leaves out the lead-in "This process involves a few steps:". The sentence now ends with a full stop, so the four-step list in entries 58-61 is no longer introduced as the steps of the optimization. Entry 66 turns "defined in terms of the virtual qubits" into "dinyatakan dalam basis virtual qubit". In quantum computing "basis" means something specific, so the wording is a little off, though it will not seriously mislead a learner. It also uses "tata letak qubit" and then "layout ini" for the same thing within one paragraph.

examples.source: Before running the circuit on hardware, optimize it for hardware execution. This process involves a few steps:
examples.translation: Sebelum menjalankan Circuit di perangkat keras, optimalkan dulu untuk eksekusi di perangkat keras.
examples.suggested: Sebelum menjalankan Circuit di perangkat keras, optimalkan dulu untuk eksekusi di perangkat keras. Proses ini melibatkan beberapa langkah:
examples.why: The dropped lead-in is what introduces the following list (entries 58-61) as the steps of this process. Without it the list has nothing introducing it.

examples.source: Your observable is also defined in terms of the virtual qubits
examples.translation: Observabelmu juga dinyatakan dalam basis virtual qubit
examples.suggested: Observabelmu juga didefinisikan berdasarkan virtual qubit
examples.why: 'basis' is a loaded quantum term (measurement/computational basis) that the English does not use here. The paragraph also switches between 'tata letak qubit' and 'layout'.

editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries (6, 15, 36, 54, 61) would mislead a learner. The upper-bound guarantee in [61], the "under suitable assumptions" caveat in [15] and the single-circuit contrast in [36] are all intact. Three small wording issues remain. In [15], "Tutorial lain" reads as "another tutorial" when the English means "the other (related) tutorial". In [36], "satu Circuit variasional heuristik tunggal" says "single" twice. In [54], "Circuit" and "sirkuit" appear in the same sentence, and "hardware" appears where the rest of the page uses "perangkat keras".

examples.source: The other tutorial uses a heuristic variational ansatz
examples.translation: Tutorial lain menggunakan ansatz variasional heuristik
examples.suggested: Tutorial tersebut menggunakan ansatz variasional heuristik
examples.why: 'Tutorial lain' means 'another tutorial' and makes the reference vague. The English points back to the related tutorial named in the previous sentence.

examples.source: samples were drawn from a single heuristic variational circuit
examples.translation: sampel diambil dari satu Circuit variasional heuristik tunggal
examples.suggested: sampel diambil dari satu Circuit variasional heuristik saja
examples.why: 'satu ... tunggal' says 'single' twice, which reads as a translation calque.

examples.source: After optimizing the circuits for hardware execution ... sample bitstrings from each circuit
examples.translation: Setelah mengoptimalkan Circuit untuk eksekusi hardware ... dari setiap sirkuit
examples.suggested: Setelah mengoptimalkan Circuit untuk eksekusi di perangkat keras ... dari setiap Circuit
examples.why: The same sentence uses both 'Circuit' and 'sirkuit'. It also uses 'hardware' where nearby entries such as [51] use 'perangkat keras'. The terms still make sense, but the switching is noticeable.

editor_note: None of the 11 rewritten entries changes the meaning. The spinon-continuum bounds, the 6+4 of 20 compression plan, max_bond=128 and the caveat that estimator_options replaces the defaults instead of merging (entry 56) all match the English. There are two small style problems. Entry 50 says "lebih terbelit/entangled", which is a translator's slash hedge, and entry 56 just says "entanglement lebih tinggi" for the same idea. Entry 14 has "plot yang mengikuti", a calque of "the plots that follow"; "plot berikut" reads more natively.

examples.source: a deeper ansatz for the later, more-entangled steps
examples.translation: ansatz lebih dalam untuk langkah-langkah berikutnya yang lebih terbelit/entangled
examples.suggested: ansatz lebih dalam untuk langkah-langkah berikutnya yang entanglement-nya lebih tinggi
examples.why: The slash gloss is a translator's hedge, not published prose, and entry 56 already says 'entanglement lebih tinggi' for the same idea.

examples.source: Those are the dashed curves on the plots that follow.
examples.translation: Itulah kurva putus-putus pada plot yang mengikuti.
examples.suggested: Kedua batas ini ditampilkan sebagai kurva putus-putus pada plot berikut.
examples.why: 'yang mengikuti' copies the English 'that follow'. Indonesian technical writing uses 'berikut'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, and nothing would mislead a learner. The physics caveats hold: the GS magnetization of zero removes the need to subtract, the paper's J is a factor of 2 off, and the two-layer AQC fidelity is lower without that being a regression. Terminology is inconsistent across the file: circuit appears as both 'sirkuit' and 'circuit', ground state as both 'keadaan dasar' and 'ground-state', observable as both 'Observable' and 'Observabel', and entangled/entanglement as both 'terbelit' and 'entanglement'. Entry [16] reads like half-translated MT ('Neutron scattering', 'sustainability', 'pengukuran scattering', 'toolkit'), even though entry [18] already uses 'hamburan neutron'. There are smaller calques too: 'Ini diharapkan' for 'This is expected' in [69], and 'exactly' is rendered as 'secara tepat'/'yang tepat' in [54]/[60] but as 'secara eksak' in [35].

examples.source: Neutron scattering helps researchers characterize materials relevant to sustainability ... connect theoretical models to scattering measurements.
examples.translation: Neutron scattering membantu peneliti mengkarakterisasi material yang relevan dengan sustainability ... dengan pengukuran scattering.
examples.suggested: Hamburan neutron membantu peneliti mengkarakterisasi material yang relevan dengan keberlanjutan ... dengan pengukuran hamburan.
examples.why: This paragraph is half untranslated, which clashes with the 'hamburan neutron' used everywhere else in the file.

examples.source: both ground-state preparation ... and circuit-level time evolution
examples.translation: persiapan ground-state ... evolusi waktu tingkat circuit
examples.suggested: penyiapan keadaan dasar ... evolusi waktu tingkat sirkuit
examples.why: The file switches between 'sirkuit'/'circuit' and 'keadaan dasar'/'ground-state'. It should use one rendering for each term.

examples.source: append exact Trotter layers to the optimized two-layer AQC circuit
examples.translation: tambahkan lapisan Trotter yang tepat ke circuit AQC dua lapisan
examples.suggested: tambahkan lapisan Trotter eksak ke sirkuit AQC dua lapisan
examples.why: 'yang tepat' can be read as 'the appropriate' rather than 'exact, not approximated'. Entry [35] already uses 'secara eksak'.

examples.source: This is expected, and you can improve these fidelities
examples.translation: Ini diharapkan, dan Anda dapat meningkatkan fidelitas ini
examples.suggested: Hal ini memang wajar, dan Anda dapat meningkatkan fidelitas ini
examples.why: 'Ini diharapkan' is a calque that sounds like 'this is hoped for' and does not carry the sense of 'this is to be expected'.

editor_note: All 8 rewritten entries say the same thing as the English and none would mislead a learner. The numbers carry over correctly: about 100 vs about 10 iterations in [24], and 'deviasi kuadrat' in [15]. Entry [191] translates 'noisy hardware' as 'perangkat keras berderau', but the rest of the page uses 'bising' ([109] 'masih bising', [126] 'perangkat kuantum yang bising'), so the adjective should match. Entry [121] drops the English bold on **local search**, which was the term the following bullet list defines.

examples.source: making quantum optimization practical on today's noisy hardware
examples.translation: membuat optimasi kuantum praktis di perangkat keras berderau saat ini
examples.suggested: membuat optimasi kuantum praktis di perangkat keras kuantum saat ini yang masih bising
examples.why: The rest of the page renders 'noisy' as 'bising' ([109], [126]). 'berderau' is a valid word, but using it only here breaks consistency.

examples.source: Iskay performs classical **local search** post-processing:
examples.translation: Iskay melakukan post-processing klasik berupa local search:
examples.suggested: Iskay melakukan post-processing klasik berupa **local search**:
examples.why: The English bolds the key term that the next bullet list explains. The translation drops that emphasis.

editor_note: The five rewritten entries match the English and none would mislead a learner. For example, entry 81 keeps the CNOT control logic intact ("Jika qubit kontrol berada dalam keadaan $|0\rangle$, gate identitas $I$ diterapkan ke target … $|1\rangle$, gate X diterapkan"), and entries 12, 15 and 41 keep the informal "kamu" register throughout.

All four rewritten entries (88, 105, 134, 166) keep the English meaning, with no drift or hallucination. Entry 88 reads 'pasca-proses (postprocess)… mitigasi error pengukuran atau zero noise extrapolation (ZNE)', entry 105 keeps the ⟨Z₀Zᵢ⟩ correlation framing intact, and entry 134 correctly renders 'family of functions' as 'sekumpulan fungsi'. One small fix remains: entry 166 leaves 'Bloch sphere' in English ('di Bloch sphere ketiga'), but entry 22 on the same page already uses the Indonesian 'bola Bloch'. A native editor would bring 166 in line with that.

examples.source: represented in the third Bloch sphere, points along the x-axis
examples.translation: yang direpresentasikan di Bloch sphere ketiga, menunjuk ke arah sumbu-x
examples.suggested: yang direpresentasikan di bola Bloch ketiga, menunjuk ke arah sumbu-x
examples.why: Entry 22 on the same page renders the term as 'bola Bloch'. Leaving it in English here is a within-file inconsistency and makes the Indonesian prose less natural. It does not mislead.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries (15, 26, 33, 72) would mislead a learner. The reset-to-|0〉 behaviour, the deterministic `reset` and the effect of scale and depth on fidelity all keep their meaning. Three wording slips remain. Entry 33 keeps the English impersonal "one often measures" as "seseorang sering mengukur", which is a calque; a passive would read more naturally. Entry 15 says "takluk oleh dekoherensi" where Indonesian would say "takluk pada/terhadap". Entry 72 turns "noise scaling" into a wordy gloss plus a redundant parenthetical, "bagaimana noise ikut membesar (penskalaan noise)".

examples.source: one often measures a qubit and then resets it for reuse
examples.translation: seseorang sering mengukur qubit lalu meresetnya untuk digunakan kembali
examples.suggested: qubit sering diukur lalu direset agar dapat digunakan kembali
examples.why: 'seseorang' copies the English impersonal 'one'. Indonesian technical prose would use a passive here.

examples.source: succumbs to decoherence and errors
examples.translation: takluk oleh dekoherensi dan kesalahan
examples.suggested: takluk pada dekoherensi dan kesalahan
examples.why: 'takluk' normally takes 'pada/terhadap'. 'takluk oleh' sounds off.

examples.source: understanding noise scaling
examples.translation: memahami bagaimana noise ikut membesar (penskalaan noise)
examples.suggested: memahami bagaimana noise bertambah seiring skala sistem
examples.why: The paraphrase and the parenthetical term say the same thing twice. This makes a short summary bullet wordy.
